requirements.requirement: Establish redundant routing across two independent transit networks between node1 (VyOS) and node2 (OPNsense) so node3's and node4's private subnets can reach each other
requirements.summary: VyOS configured with floating static routes to node4's subnet via both transit next-hops (distance 1/10, interface-pinned) and a forward-filter with explicit accepts; OPNsense configured with opt1/opt2/opt3 interfaces, GW_T1/GW_T2 gateways with dpinger monitoring, firewall pass rules, and a static route to node3's subnet kept current by a failover script/cron. End-to-end ping node3->node4 succeeded 5/5 after this was in place.

requirements.requirement: Traffic continues to flow between the two private networks when one transit network is taken out of service, demonstrated across the actual transition
requirements.summary: A continuous background ping from node3 was running when transit1 was administratively downed on both node1 (eth1 disable) and node2 (vtnet1 down); the VyOS RIB and OPNsense static route both switched to transit2, and the ping log showed only a brief gap (~4 missed 0.3s-interval probes, roughly ~1.2s) rather than a sustained outage, confirming live failover rather than a pre-configured static test.

requirements.requirement: Restoration of the failed transit network and reconvergence back onto it is shown
requirements.summary: eth1/vtnet1 were re-enabled, VyOS's RIB and OPNsense's static route both reverted automatically to the transit1 gateway, and a final ping showed 0% packet loss, confirming reconvergence.

overall_summary: The executor built dual-transit static routing (VyOS floating routes plus OPNsense dpinger-monitored gateways and a cron-driven failover script) that carries traffic between node3's and node4's private subnets over either of two independent transit paths. A live disruption test with a continuous background ping directly demonstrated failover to the secondary transit with only ~1.2s of loss, and a subsequent restoration test showed clean reconvergence back to the primary transit with 0% loss. All three material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct evidence. Independently, the mandated provider-wide node-restart protocol was executed on all four nodes with distinct pre/post boot identities and recovered end-to-end connectivity in each case (node3 required a second reboot after discovering and fixing a `connection.autoconnect=no` bug, which is an acceptable corrective action). Operational hygiene is generally good — most exploratory work (an initial 169.254.x addressing scheme, a non-functional gateway-group static route) was fully reverted — but the executor briefly disabled the OPNsense firewall entirely (`pfctl -d`) during troubleshooting without an explicit, deliberate re-enable step, and left a handful of stray /tmp files on node3/node4 after the reboot tests.
limitations: The pfctl -d firewall-disable on node2 was not explicitly reversed by the executor; its restoration is inferred from a later configctl filter reload/routing_configure run rather than directly confirmed with a 'pf enabled' status check immediately afterward.
Packet-loss quantification during the live failover relied on a client-side ping sequence-number gap analysis rather than a precise timestamped loss window, so the ~1.2s figure is an approximation.

Package-manager health checks on node3 and node4 timed out in all lifecycle snapshots (before_prepare and after_executor), so package-state integrity could not be independently verified before/after the executor's work.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most exploratory mutations were bounded and cleaned up: an initial link-local (169.254.x) addressing scheme on node1/node2/node3/node4 was fully flushed/reconfigured to the working 10.201.x scheme (cmd-1d38ddd222e24aa1, cmd-583bda0eb49a4832 reverted by cmd-80cfb6e9a1c645aa, cmd-0a96b01ed42442f1), and a non-functional OPNsense static-route-to-gateway-group approach (GWGRP_T route plus a route-to policy rule) was added then fully removed once discovered to be ineffective (cmd-913eb69f3d964c71, cmd-982bee8f858a4579 reverted by cmd-81f3ea21ed234441). One notable exception: the executor ran `pfctl -d` on node2 (cmd-a57205c0efe54286), fully disabling the OPNsense firewall for a diagnostic check; this is a security-control-weakening action, and although the firewall was implicitly restored a few minutes later by a legitimate `configctl filter reload`/`rc.routing_configure` invocation (cmd-a73c5982aa134403, cmd-e2e5186a4c3645b3), the executor did not explicitly re-enable pf itself, leaving a window where the perimeter filter was off. Minor residue also remained after the reboot protocol: leftover /tmp files (continuity.pid, reboot3.log, reboot3b.log, tn4.log) were not cleaned up on node3/node4 per the after_executor snapshot.
